document_summary: Massachusetts General Laws c. 186, § 18, the state anti-retaliation statute protecting tenants who report code violations, enforce housing laws, or join tenants' unions (Massachusetts).

rules.title: M.G.L. c. 186, § 18 - Tenant reprisal (anti-retaliation) protection
rules.requirement: Landlords may not threaten or take reprisals against tenants for reporting violations, enforcing housing laws, or organizing a tenants' union; a termination notice or rent increase within six months of such activity is presumed to be a reprisal.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants of residential premises; six-month rebuttable presumption applies to notices of termination (except for nonpayment of rent), rent increases, or substantial alterations in tenancy terms.
rules.quoted_span: Any waiver of this provision in any lease or other rental agreement shall be void and unenforceable.
rules.out_of_scope_reason: Anti-retaliation provision, not a limit on grounds for eviction; excluded from scope.
rules.extraction_notes: No effective date stated in the document text. Damages are one to three months' rent or actual damages plus costs and attorney's fees (penalty, not a key value).
